summary: Tested body.scrollTop-based scroll behavior on artirdim.com preview (bundle app-Dbg7Nccy.js). FORWARD navigation still works correctly on both viewports (detail_after_nav = 0). BACK-button scroll RESTORE FAILS on both desktop and mobile — document.body.scrollTop stays at 0 for the entire 3s window after browser Back, instead of restoring to the previously saved value (~1800 desktop / ~5000 mobile).

ui_bugs.issue: Browser Back does NOT restore document.body.scrollTop. Measured home_after_back = 0 on both viewports. Continuous 100ms poll for 3s after go_back() shows scrollTop = 0 the entire time — no restoration attempt ever visibly executes.

integration_issues.flow: Home → auction detail → browser Back → Home
integration_issues.issue: Scroll position lost on Back. Expected body.scrollTop > 800 (desktop) / > 1500 (mobile); got 0.

measurements.diagnostic_polling_desktop: 34 samples at 100ms intervals over ~3.5s covering pre-back, popstate, and post-back windows — every sample recorded document.body.scrollTop = 0. Peak scrollTop after go_back() = 0.

rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) Load https://laravel-vue-stream.preview.emergentagent.com. 2) Set document.body.scrollTop = 1800 (desktop) or 5000 (mobile). 3) Click a.idx-card. 4) Detail page loads at scrollTop 0 (correct). 5) Press browser Back. 6) Observe document.body.scrollTop stays 0 (BUG — should be restored to prior value).
diagnostic_evidence: history.state.key is ALWAYS null in this Inertia setup — history.state contains {page:{...}} but no 'key' field. Therefore pageKey() in app.js falls back to window.location.href. This should still work as a key because the URL is the same when returning to home.
popstate event DOES fire on Back (recorded at correct timestamp) so popState flag should be set to true.
But scrollBodyTo(y) is either (a) never invoked, (b) invoked with y=0 because scrollPositions[homeHref] was never saved, or (c) invoked but immediately overwritten by hardScrollTop().

Continuous 100ms scroll polling over 3.5s post-back showed NO transient spike — body.scrollTop never became non-zero even for a single sample, which rules out theory (c) unless overwrite happens synchronously in the same task.
most_likely_causes: A) router.on('finish') may NOT fire (or may fire with different event shape) for popstate-triggered visits in the installed Inertia version, so the restore block never runs. Verify with console.log inside the finish handler.

B) router.on('before') may not fire on the forward click either (e.g., if the link uses standard <a href> and full page reload is prevented some other way), so scrollPositions[homeHref] never gets 1800 and default is 0. Verify by logging inside the before handler.
C) The 800ms safety timeout resets popState = false before finish fires — but this would only apply if finish is delayed >800ms; unlikely to be the sole cause but possible on slow cold cache.
recommended_fixes_for_main_agent: Add temporary console.log inside router.on('before') and router.on('finish') in resources/js/app.js to verify which hooks actually fire on forward click AND on browser Back. This will identify whether the failure is at save-time or restore-time.

As a robustness measure, ALSO save scroll on 'scroll' events (throttled) into scrollPositions[currentHref], not only on 'before'. This guarantees a value exists even if 'before' does not fire for a given navigation.

In the popstate listener itself, do NOT rely on router.on('finish'); instead schedule the restore directly (e.g., requestAnimationFrame + a couple of retries at 60/120/240ms) using scrollPositions[location.href]. This decouples restoration from Inertia lifecycle timing.
Remove the 800ms popState-reset safety, or increase it, so it cannot race with a slow finish event.

Also verify that hardScrollTop() is NOT being called after the restore on popstate — the current guard (`if (popState) { ...; return; }`) looks correct, but the setTimeout(hardScrollTop, 60) inside forward path is fine; ensure no other listener (e.g., initKT / KTScroll.createInstances) is resetting body.scrollTop after arrival.

action_items: Fix browser Back scroll restoration for document.body (id=kt_app_body). Currently 0 on both desktop and mobile — should restore to the previously saved body.scrollTop value.
Add instrumentation logs to router.on('before')/router.on('finish') to determine which hook is failing, then apply a popstate-driven restore that does not depend on Inertia's finish lifecycle.
Consider throttled scroll-listener-based saving to make the saved value robust even when 'before' does not fire.
critical_code_review_comments: resources/js/app.js relies on router.on('finish') firing for popstate navigations. In some Inertia versions this hook does not fire (or fires with different flags) for cached back-nav, which appears to be the case here.

pageKey() falls back to location.href because history.state.key is null in this app — this is fine for exact-URL round-trips but will break if the URL includes changing query strings (e.g., pagination/filter state).

The 800ms popState reset in the popstate handler creates a race condition: if the Inertia visit completes after 800ms, restore won't execute. Slow networks / cold caches will silently break restoration.

success_rate.frontend: 50% (forward-nav PASS, back-restore FAIL on both viewports)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Only frontend (scroll behavior) tested. The real scroll container is document.body (id=kt_app_body). Always measure body.scrollTop, not window.scrollY. Forward nav works (detail_after_nav=0). Back-restore is broken: home_after_back=0 on 1920x800 (scrolled from 1800) and on 390x844 (scrolled from 5000). Bundle in use: app-Dbg7Nccy.js (verified contains 'scrollRestoration', 'popstate', 'kt_app_root'). history.state.key is null so pageKey() falls back to location.href.
